dimension: COUNTER — counter, serving bays and galley
method_summary:
NO HERO AND NO out/ EXIST, so every finding is SOURCE-vs-PHOTOGRAPH. Nothing was built, nothing was written into /home/user/tacombi; all scratch work is in the session scratchpad. Read: t1_detail.py (CANTILEVERED COUNTER header, plank_counter, _counter_outer/_counter_inner, counter_nosing, _counter_tan, counter_top, galley, galley_dressing, menu_cards, bobble_fringe, spec4_details), t1_shell.py (BAY_W/BAY_CX/BAYS/B_PILLAR/DOOR_REAR_DX), t1_mats.py (COUNTERTAN/counter_tan), studio.py (the fill_galley block), build.py, verify.py (_bounds skip list), STATE.md, AUDIT_rev11/12, REF_MEASUREMENTS sec.4-6, SPEC 10.15/10.19/10.99.6.

MEASUREMENT: /tmp/blender/4.5/python/bin/python3.11 with PIL+numpy on ref_side.jpg and ref_rear34.jpg only (read-only; scripts in the scratchpad: bay1.py bay2.py bay3.py final.py pill.py pill2.py disp.py cadh.py fr2.py gold.py cfwd.py geo.py ruler.py).

THE ONLY RULER USED IS THE LOCKED BAY_W = 0.5155 m, read on each bay's OWN half-max cut edges. No ground line (10.11), no bumper/lamppost origin, no cab-door plane (10.62/10.73), no absolute px/m carried across the frame. Local scale comes out 198.5 / 203.5 / 211.8 px/m at bays 1/2/3; REF sec.4's band heights give 202.5 / 211.4 / 219.9 px/m on the INDEPENDENT vertical axis, and the two axes agree on the growth (1.067 vs 1.086), which corroborates the settled reading that the aperture-width taper is perspective. BLIND VALIDATION of the ruler on a feature nothing was tuned against: it predicts the counter's forward end (CNT_X0 = 0.9180) at image x 325.9; the first continuous column of gold-nosing pixels in ref_side.jpg is x = 326 +/- 3. Where only a count or an ordering is needed I used no ruler at all.

Contrast: studio.py's own printed photograph windows (bay1 u[332,422] v[330,399], bay2 u[463,554] v[325,393], bay3 u[596,689] v[319,388]) reproduce to 0.2-0.5 sd units, so the windows are the same rectangles. ref_rear34.jpg used ONLY for counts and for the presence/absence of features (SPEC 10.15/10.19 — no number taken off it). NOT touched, per instruction: CNT_ZT, CNT_ZB, CNT_NOSE_F, fascia depth (10.99.6 read first), bay widths, the tyre, the counter slab, the signboard, the withdrawn over-rider.

findings.title: menucard0 hangs across the open mouth of serving bay 1 — 61.5% of it is over the hole
findings.reference_shows: ref_side.jpg, the pillar forward of aperture 1: the first printed menu card occupies image x 303-321, entirely inside the 27 px pillar between the cab-door shutline (x 296) and aperture 1's cut edge (x 323.5 by half-max). Visible unoccluded at 7x in the crop (290,340)-(460,420): a portrait card with a red header and printed rows, with cream pillar margin on both sides and no part of it over the aperture. The same holds for the other two cards at x 433-453 and x 563-583.
findings.model_does: t1_detail.menu_cards() builds card 0 at xs[0] = (t1_shell.BAYS[0][1] + 0.9080)/2 = +0.91888. With CARD_W = 0.0948 the card spans X +0.8715 to +0.9663. BAYS[0] is (+0.41425, +0.92975) and OPEN_BAYS includes 0, so 58.3 mm of the card's 94.8 mm width lies over bay 1's OPEN aperture, 12.0 mm on the real pillar, and 24.5 mm forward of the door's rear edge (BAYS[0][1] + B_PILLAR = 0.94175) i.e. on the cab door itself. Its z span 1.3976-1.7358 is inside the band, so the overhang holds over 87% of the card's height. conform_solid() places it from the ANALYTIC flank_y(), not by ray-casting the built shell, so the hole is invisible to the placement: the card is a 4 mm slab floating 2 mm proud of nothing.
findings.method: Pure arithmetic on the shipped constants (scratchpad/geo.py), plus git archaeology for the cause. The literal 0.9080 is a bare number that did not move when rev 13 (ac51f10) replaced BAYS = [(0.3130,0.8200),...] with BAY_W/BAY_CX: BAYS[0][1] went 0.8200 -> 0.92975, so the pillar the card was authored into moved +110 mm while the card's centre moved only +55 mm. Before rev 13 the card sat on an 88.0 mm pillar with 3.4 mm proud each side, which is exactly what the docstring's 'built +0.864' records — that figure is now stale by 55 mm and still published. Cards 1 and 2 are expressed wholly in terms of BAYS and are correctly inside their pillars (7.5 mm and 32 mm margins), so the defect is one literal. Uncertainty: none — this is not a measurement, it is the model's own numbers. The only judgement is the photograph's ordinal fact that the card sits on the pillar, and that is unambiguous at 7x.
findings.fix_location: t1_detail.py :: menu_cards() — the first element of xs, the bare literal 0.9080; express it in terms of t1_shell.BAYS[0][1] + B_PILLAR the way DOOR_REAR_DX already is

findings.title: Bay 1's published contrast AND mean targets are a man in a white shirt; the fill wattage was chosen against the contaminated mean
findings.reference_shows: ref_side.jpg, bay 1, window u[332,422] v[330,399]: a man fills it — bare forearm crossing the full width at v 344-363, white printed shirt over the right two thirds and the lower half. 272 of the window's 6370 pixels exceed 210 DN and 99.6% of them lie at x >= 364, on that torso. Bays 2 and 3 contain no person (verified at 8x): bay 2 shows a red-lettered price list, a shelf, a green and a white item; bay 3 shows hanging pale strips, a flat wall and a yellow bottle.
findings.model_does: studio.views() prints, as the shipped acceptance row, 'ref_side.jpg sd 33.69+-0.99 / 24.16+-0.76 / 21.36+-1.38, photo means 147.7 / 158.0 / 178.3', and selects the per-bay fill _gw = (0.25, 0.0, 0.29) with the stated reason 'bay 1's mean lands on 147.1 against 147.7'. t1_detail.galley_dressing()'s '6b. INTERNAL CONTRAST' block still states 'bay 1 renders sd 15.3 against the photograph's 28.4' and derives four galley panels from a 28.4 ceiling. Both targets are the contaminated statistic.
findings.method: Re-derived four ways on the same window (scratchpad/final.py). Spatial man mask (u >= 364, plus the arm band located per column by its dark core, no threshold on brightness — 70.5% of the window): surviving pixels sd 19.00 mean 133.29; forward strip u 332-363 only sd 19.16 mean 131.52; iid-resample inpaint over the full window sd 19.00 +- 0.14 (200 trials); mirrored-strip inpaint sd 18.98 mean 132.31. TRUE PER-BAY PHOTOGRAPH FIGURES: bay 1 sd 19.0 +- 1.0 at mean 132.4 +- 1.0; bay 2 sd 24.5 +- 0.8 at mean 157.4 (uncontaminated and inset-stable, 24.53 -> 24.07 over 0-8 px extra inset); bay 3 sd 20.4 +- 1.5 at mean 177.5 (the least determined — it falls monotonically 21.87 -> 18.94 over the same inset sweep, which is why AUDIT_rev12 read 18.43 +- 1.43 and studio.py read 21.36; both are right on their own window). So the published bay-1 sd target is +77% and the published bay-1 mean target is +11.6% (147.8 vs 132.4, +15.4 DN). ORDINAL CONSEQUENCE, needing no ruler: studio.py's own sweep shows the fill RAISES bay 1's mean monotonically (0.25 W -> 147.1, 0.40 -> 152.2, 0.60 -> 157.9), so T1_FILLG1 = 0.25 was set on the WRONG SIDE of the true target — the correction is downward and larger than the whole swept range. SECOND ORDINAL: the photograph ranks the bays 2 > 3 > 1 (24.5 > 20.4 > 19.0); the published row ranks them 1 > 2 > 3. The rig was tuned against a ranking whose top member is a person. CEILING ON THIS ITEM: the render side is NOT MEASURABLE (no hero), so the size of the rendered error is not established here — only that the target is wrong by 15.4 DN and the lever's sign is known.
findings.fix_location: studio.py :: views(), the fill_galley block — the _gw / T1_FILLG1 default and the A/B target row in its comment; and t1_detail.py :: galley_dressing(), the '6b. INTERNAL CONTRAST' block's 28.4 ceiling

findings.title: The counter carries two condiment caddies; no supplied frame shows fewer than four, and ref_side.jpg shows five
findings.reference_shows: ref_side.jpg: FIVE identical napkin dispensers stand in one rank on the counter top under the '100% Calidad' sunburst. Their steel side frames give five dark minima at x = 715, 737, 761, 786, 808 with the fifth box ending at x = 831 (mean of rows 372-397, scratchpad/disp.py); the profile is featureless cream from 833 onward. Boxes 716-735, 740-757, 762-780, 788-805, 812-830; pitch 23.25 px, box 21 px, gap 2.3 px. ref_rear34.jpg (counts only, no number taken) shows the same rank at x 772-904 and resolves FOUR boxes.
findings.model_does: t1_detail.galley_dressing() section 7 builds exactly two: 'for i, (bx0, bx1) in enumerate(((-1.0420, -1.1550), (-1.1600, -1.2730)))' -> gal_caddy0/1 plus gal_caddy_fill0/1. Its own comment names the measurement window: 'two stainless caddies aft of it, image x 715-760'. That window ends at 760, i.e. inside the gap between box 2 and box 3 of a rank that runs to 831.
findings.method: The headline is a COUNT and needs no ruler: 2 built against 5 in the primary frame and 4 in the secondary. The transience of counter props (the two frames disagree, 5 vs 4) does not rescue 2 — no frame shows two. Scale-free supporting metrics, taken as ratios to bay 3's own locked width (109.17 px = 0.5155 m, 3 px aft of the rank): the photographic rank spans 115.5 px = 1.058 bay-widths = 0.545 m; the model's two caddies span 0.231 m, i.e. 42% of the rank, leaving 0.31 m of counter bare where three boxes stand. Per-unit the model is close: pitch 0.118 m built against 0.110 m measured (+7%), width 0.113 against 0.099 (+14%). One aspect error: box height/pitch is fully scale-free (both lengths on the same plane) and reads 24 +- 2 px / 23.25 +- 0.5 px = 1.03 +- 0.10 in the photograph against 0.155/0.118 = 1.31 built, +27%. The caddies are therefore too few and each ~27% too tall for its footprint. This is the same failure family as the mask that dropped 14% of the ink: a measurement window edge, not the object, decided the answer.
findings.fix_location: t1_detail.py :: galley_dressing(), section 7 — the gal_caddy{i} loop's two-tuple of (bx0, bx1) spans, and the 'image x 715-760' window in its comment

findings.title: The forward half of the counter is bare in the model; the standing 'CLUTTER ON THE COUNTER' instruction is answered only aft of X = -0.686
findings.reference_shows: ref_side.jpg: a tip box stands on the counter at image x 421-437, y 397-417 — a pale rectangular box ~16 x 21 px lettered 'TIPS', directly outboard of the pillar between bays 1 and 2 (crop (290,340)-(460,420) at 7x). ref_rear34.jpg (presence only) shows the counter's forward run carrying a stack of pale plates, a shallow round dish, a small pale item and a tall green can. Both frames show the forward run dressed.
findings.model_does: t1_detail.galley_dressing()'s section 7 is headed 'counter top, show side (EXTERIOR props)' and its forward-most object is gal_warmer at X -0.6860. plank_counter() runs the slab from CNT_X0 = +0.9180 to CNT_X1 = T.X_TAIL - CNT_OVERHANG = -2.1880. Nothing whatever stands on the 1.604 m from +0.918 to -0.686 — 51.6% of the counter's length. build.py calls only plank_counter, galley and spec4_details, so there is no other source of counter props.
findings.method: Model side is a census of the built objects and their authored X spans, not a measurement. Photograph side: the tip box's station comes from the validated in-plane ruler (bay 1's locked width, local 199.7 px/m interpolated between bays 1 and 2), giving X = +0.36 to +0.44, i.e. squarely on the pillar-1 station — no absolute px/m or origin used. The 51.6% figure is exact arithmetic on the shipped constants (scratchpad/geo.py). NOTE ON HONESTY: counter props are transient and the two frames disagree in detail, so I do not claim any specific missing object beyond the tip box; the ORDINAL claim is that both frames show the forward run dressed and the model has it completely bare, which is the owner's raised-more-than-once complaint restated. Rev 11's answer to that complaint was 55 objects INSIDE the galley, behind the apertures; the counter itself got four objects and all four are in its aft third.
findings.fix_location: t1_detail.py :: galley_dressing(), section 7 (counter top, show side) — it needs entries forward of gal_warmer, starting with the tip box at X ~ +0.40

findings.title: The two inter-bay pillars are 109.5 and 129.5 mm; the photograph's are equal, and the model's asymmetry has the wrong sign
findings.reference_shows: ref_side.jpg, the sheet metal between the serving apertures. Half-max cut edges on rows 330-360 (chosen above the menu cards and above the white shirt that corrupts the lower rows): aperture edges at 323.5 / 425.8, 454.0 / 558.9, 587.5 / 696.7; pillar 1 = 28.4 px, pillar 2 = 29.0 px. Ratio p2/p1 = 1.02. REF sec.4's independent 8x read of the outer dark outline gives 25 px and 24 px, ratio 0.96. Both conventions say the two pillars are equal to within a couple of percent.
findings.model_does: t1_shell.BAYS is built from BAY_CX = (0.6720, 0.0470, -0.5980) with the equal BAY_W = 0.5155, giving BAYS = [(0.41425, 0.92975), (-0.21075, 0.30475), (-0.85575, -0.34025)]. Pillar 1 = 0.1095 m, pillar 2 = 0.1295 m — differing by 20.0 mm, ratio 1.183, with the AFT pillar the wider. The 20 mm is exactly BAY_CX's centre-spacing asymmetry (0.6250 vs 0.6450); with the widths equalised in rev 13 it has nowhere to go but the pillars. Before rev 13 the unequal extents absorbed it and the pillars read 0.1180 / 0.1140 — REF sec.4's numbers exactly.
findings.method: The ORDINAL core needs no ruler and survives both edge conventions: photograph pillars equal within 2%, model differ by 18% with the sign inverted. The METRIC is a ratio to the locked BAY_W with the scale interpolated from the two bays that bracket each pillar, so no absolute px/m and no origin: P1 = 515.5 x 28.4/103.6 = 141 mm, P2 = 515.5 x 29.0/107.1 = 140 mm, +-5 mm from +-0.5 px per edge. On REF's outer-dark-outline convention the same arithmetic gives ~124 and ~116 mm. The conventions differ by ~17 mm, so the SAFE metric claim is pillar 1 only: too narrow by 12 to 32 mm on every convention tested. Cross-check that does not use the pillar edges at all: perspective-corrected aperture centre spacings are 0.6558 and 0.6537 m (equal to 2.2 mm) against BAY_CX's 0.6250 and 0.6450. The raw pixel centre-spacing ratio agrees (photo 1.0297, model 1.0320) only because a real 3.2% geometric asymmetry is standing in for 3.4% of perspective — the retired taper removed from the WIDTHS, still present in the CENTRES. BAY_W is guarded every revision (verify prints 0.516 0.515 0.516); BAY_CX is guarded by nothing.
findings.fix_location: t1_shell.py :: BAY_CX — the centre spacings 0.6250 / 0.6450 were not re-derived when BAY_W was equalised in rev 13

findings.title: The aperture bobble fringe is pitched 26.0 mm against 32.4 mm measured — ~13 extra balls per aperture, 39 across the three
findings.reference_shows: ref_side.jpg resolves the fringe cleanly along the bottom run of bays 1 and 2 (crop (455,390)-(570,408) at 10x shows individually separated white bobbles on their tape). Dominant along-run period on rows 396-401 of bay 2: 6.67 px from a 9-interval peak fit over x 489-549; bay 1 gives 6.38 px over 8 intervals on rows 398-404. FFT on both runs returns the same 6.62 px bin.
findings.model_does: t1_detail.FRINGE_PITCH = 0.0260 with FRINGE_R = 0.0090 and FRINGE_INSET = 0.0130, consumed by bobble_fringe() through _resample_closed(). On the offset bay outline (perimeter 1.661 m) that is 64 balls per aperture, three apertures.
findings.method: Converted as a RATIO to the locked BAY_W on the SAME bay the pitch was read on — pitch/width is dimensionless, so no px/m, no origin, no ground line, and it is immune to the outboard-parallax term that SPEC 10.99.6 caught (both lengths lie on one plane). Bay 2: 6.667/104.93 x 515.5 = 32.8 mm. Bay 1: 6.375/102.31 x 515.5 = 32.1 mm. Combined 32.4 +- 2.0 mm (the band is dominated by the +-0.3 px period estimate). Built 26.0 mm is 20% too fine, 3.2 sigma. This independently reproduces AUDIT_rev12's 31.1 +- 1.0 mm by a different method on a different bay, and that finding is still unapplied 30 revisions later. Consequence in counted units: 64 balls per aperture built against 51 at the measured pitch. NOT claimed: ball DIAMETER — at 4-6 px it is blur-dominated, and the pitch is a periodicity that blur cannot move.
findings.fix_location: t1_detail.py :: FRINGE_PITCH (consumed by bobble_fringe via _resample_closed)

findings.title: Nothing in the model stands on the counter's 315 mm tail overhang, and the four squeeze bottles that claim to are all forward of the tail
findings.reference_shows: ref_side.jpg: the counter's tail overhang is unoccluded past the body's rear corner and carries an object — a pale tray with small upright items at image x 914-942, y 372-398, sitting on the tan top inboard of the gold nosing (crop (810,300)-(1010,430) at 5x, which also confirms the radiused corner and the nosing running continuously round it). Over the run x 834-910 the counter is bare in this frame: the 11x crop (820,355)-(910,415) is featureless cream between the fifth dispenser and the corner. ref_rear34.jpg (presence only) does show four squeeze bottles with red and yellow caps, standing immediately aft of the dispenser rank.
findings.model_does: t1_detail.galley_dressing() builds gal_bot0..3 / gal_botcap0..3 at X = -1.860, -1.925, -1.990, -2.055 plus _dtail = T.X_TAIL - T.X_TAIL_OLD = +0.235, i.e. X -1.625 to -1.820, under a comment that says 'these stand on the counter's TAIL RUN'. T.X_TAIL is -1.873, so all four are FORWARD of the rearmost sheet metal by 53 to 248 mm. CNT_X1 = -2.188, so the 315 mm of counter that actually overhangs the tail (plus the CNT_R = 0.150 corner wrap) carries nothing at all.
findings.method: The model side is arithmetic on the shipped constants — no measurement, and the code's own prose contradicts its own coordinates. The photograph side is deliberately ORDINAL only: I do not convert x 914-942 to a model X, because that station is 200+ px aft of the last bay, the flank's px/m is documented as non-constant there, and the object sits on the counter's outboard plane where SPEC 10.99.6's parallax term bites. What is safe is the ordering: an object stands aft of the body's rearmost sheet metal, and the model's aftmost counter prop stands forward of it. LOWEST CONFIDENCE OF MY SEVEN, and stated as such: counter props are transient, ref_side and ref_rear34 disagree about the bottles' presence, and the bottles came from ref_rear34, which SPEC 10.15 quarantines and 10.19 only partly releases. I am not asking for the bottles to be deleted — I am reporting that the tail overhang, which the build spent a constant (CNT_OVERHANG) to get right, is undressed in both the model and the code's own description.
findings.fix_location: t1_detail.py :: galley_dressing(), the gal_bot{i} loop — the station list and the 'TAIL RUN' claim in its comment

not_measurable.title: Every per-bay RENDERED statistic — sd, mean, and whether the bays now match the photograph
not_measurable.why: There is no hero and no out/ directory in this tree, and I am barred from building one. studio.py's A/B table (render sd 23.63 / 23.44 / 21.85) is a CODE COMMENT, not a measurement I can make, and this project has published a comment as a figure before. I therefore fixed the photograph's side of the comparison and left the model's side open. The corrected photograph targets are in finding 2; what the renders do against them is unresolved and cannot be resolved here.

not_measurable.title: The X extent of bay 2's printed matter, and any comparison of what is INSIDE a bay by X
not_measurable.why: ref_side.jpg gives red printed matter in every column of bay 2's window (652 red pixels, 10.3% of it, in bands at v 325-360 and v 370-385), and galley_dressing() builds it as gal_can_u0/1/2 and gal_can_l0/1 flat on the back wall. But the two cannot be compared: galley_dressing()'s own docstring states that DEPTH (Y) IS NOT MEASURABLE in either frame, and without a depth an image-plane column cannot be converted to a back-wall X. Comparing them anyway would be exactly the scope error SPEC 10.99.6 refused. A frame that shows the galley's back wall obliquely, or an owner statement on the depth, would settle it.

not_measurable.title: The counter's outboard projection CNT_Y_OUT (built 1.1660, i.e. ~294 mm proud of the flank)
not_measurable.why: Already established in AUDIT_rev12 sec.4 item 2 and confirmed here: ref_side.jpg is an elevation and the counter-top/flank boundary carries no step — saturation ramps monotonically. I re-checked the same rows and found the same ramp. Cited, not re-run.

not_measurable.title: COUNTERTAN's LEVEL (still bracketed -16%/+15%)
not_measurable.why: The tie-break needs a same-light, same-class, HORIZONTAL, unclipped reference lying ON the counter. I checked the only new candidates my own crops turned up — the five napkin dispensers' white fronts — and they peak at 246-255 DN with pixels at 255, i.e. clipped, exactly as the dispensers were rejected in AUDIT_rev12. The bracket stands.

not_measurable.title: The brass nosing's PROJECTION (7.0 mm) and its rolled section
not_measurable.why: ref_side.jpg is an elevation and cannot measure a Y offset; the roll was inferred from a saturation ramp on few clean columns. ref_rear34.jpg shows the nosing obliquely and confirms it is a substantial band wrapping the radiused tail corner continuously, but SPEC 10.15/10.19 leave its numbers suspect and I took none.

not_measurable.title: CNT_R (tail corner radius, 0.150) and CNT_CH (front outer chamfer, 0.050), and whether the counter has end caps
not_measurable.why: Both frames confirm the corner is RADIUSED rather than mitred and that the gold nosing follows it — that much is ordinal and the build is right. The radius itself is seen at ~18 px of strongly foreshortened arc in ref_side.jpg and obliquely in ref_rear34.jpg; neither supports a number. The counter's forward end face is small and distant in the only frame that sees it. t1_detail already labels both INFERRED, correctly.

not_measurable.title: The identity of the five counter-top boxes, and of the tray on the tail overhang
not_measurable.why: At 21 x 24 px per box in a 4:2:0 frame the class (napkin dispenser, condiment caddy, sugar station) is not recoverable — only the count, the pitch and the aspect are, and those are in finding 3. The build's choice to model them as generic stainless caddies with a pale fill is the right kind of restraint; it is the COUNT that is wrong, not the identity.

not_measurable.title: The B-pillar between the cab door and aperture 1 (B_PILLAR = 0.0120)
not_measurable.why: ref_side.jpg gives 27 px between the cab-door shutline and aperture 1's cut edge, which through bay 1's own locked width is ~136 mm against the authored 12 mm. I am NOT reporting that as a finding: the cab door in this frame is swung open ~49 degrees, so the 'shutline' at x 296 is the door's aperture edge and not the door's rear edge, and SPEC 10.62/10.73 bar any px/m on the door plane. t1_shell already says THE B-PILLAR'S TRUE WIDTH IS OPEN AND UNMEASURED and declines to take a number from ref_workshop.jpg for the same reason. It stays open. (Note this is a different quantity from finding 1, which needs no B-pillar value at all — only that the card is 61.5% over a hole.)

ceiling_statement: Positions and lengths on the show flank: +-3 to +-5 mm, set by +-0.5 px half-max edge location converted through the ONE locked in-plane ruler (BAY_W = 0.5155 m read on each bay's own edges). That ruler was validated blind — it predicts the counter's forward end at image x 325.9 against an observed 326 +/- 3 — and it never leaves the flank plane, so it is untouched by SPEC 10.11's ground line, 10.62/10.73's door plane, and 10.99.6's outboard-parallax term. Counts and orderings: exact, no ruler involved. The photograph's per-bay contrast: sd to +-1.0 DN (four estimators spanning 0.18, plus +-0.9 for +-3 px window placement) — except bay 3, which is estimator-limited to +-1.5 because its sd falls 21.9 -> 18.9 across an 8 px inset sweep. Ratios of two lengths on one plane (fringe pitch/bay width, caddy height/pitch): limited only by the edge error, ~2%. HARD CEILING ON THE WHOLE REPORT: no finding here is confirmed against a picture of the model. There is no hero and no out/, so every claim is SOURCE-vs-PHOTOGRAPH — I can prove what the build CONSTRUCTS and what the photograph SHOWS, and I cannot prove what either LOOKS LIKE. Findings 1, 3, 4 and 7 are immune to that ceiling because they are counts, spans and topology in the model's own coordinates; findings 2, 5 and 6 name a wrong constant, not a wrong picture.

dimension: WHEELS — wheels, tyres, arches, contact shadow (+ the assigned ride-height adjudication)
method_summary: READ-ONLY throughout; `git status` shows no modified tracked file (only other agents' untracked PNGs), so verify_clone.sh is untouched. All scripts were written to the session scratchpad, never to /home/user/tacombi. Measurement with /tmp/blender/4.5/python/bin/python3.11 (numpy + PIL) on ref_side.jpg and ref_workshop.jpg. Edge criterion throughout: bilinear resample along a ray or column, 5-tap binomial smooth, parabolic peak of |dL/ds| — a criterion that is background-LEVEL independent for a step, chosen because AUDIT_rev12 §22 refuted the previous fixed L-band mask for being a different criterion on every background. ONE RULER ONLY, and it never leaves the wheel: the rear wheel's own free tyre diameter (locked TYRE_D 0.665). NO GROUND LINE ENTERS ANY NUMBER I PUBLISH (§10.11), no px/m is imported from the flank, no cab-door plane is used (§10.62/10.73), the Z-ladder is not quoted (§10.99), ref_rear34 is not used at all (§10.15), and no livery/weathering claim is taken off ref_workshop. Chain: (1) rear rim flange fitted by 357 rays, circle centre (749.271, 604.138), R 46.427 px, rms 0.339 px — this is the hub datum and the only datum. (2) Free tyre radius three ways: upper-arc max-gradient over 140 rays (70.62, rms 0.80), free circle fit (70.52, centre concentric with the rim to 0.36 px), and flange × the built TIRE_R/RIM_R (70.23) → adopt 70.43 ± 0.25 px. (3) Tyre bottom by column scan, 15 columns u 715–785. (4) Rear arch lip by R-channel edge, 21 columns u 700–800. (5) Front-vs-rear rim flange refitted as axis-aligned ellipses to test steer. findings.title: The tyres do not deform at the contact patch, so the whole vehicle stands 28.6 mm too high above its own ground plane — and this is the one ride-height term no hub-referenced measurement can see
findings.reference_shows: ref_side.jpg, rear wheel. Above and beside the hub the tyre outline is a circle: 140 rays over 178–255° and 280–345°, max-gradient edge, free-fit R = 70.52 px at rms 0.80 px with its centre 0.36 px from the rim-flange centre. BELOW the hub it is FLAT: column scans at u = 715,720,...,785 put the tyre/ground boundary at v = 667.2–668.7 (spread 0.7 px over 70 px = 0.331 m of straight line), where that same circle would reach v = 674.8 at u = 750. Half-max crossings on the same columns give 668.8 ± 0.3; max-gradient gives 668.3 ± 0.5. The flat's two ends rejoin the circle within 1.2–1.4 px at u = 715 and u = 785, and beyond them the dark boundary drops BELOW the circle (contact shadow on the paving) — the opposite sign, so shadow cannot have manufactured the flat. Free radius 70.43 ± 0.25 px, loaded radius 64.36 ± 0.40 px, deflection 6.06 ± 0.47 px = 28.6 ± 2.3 mm. Loaded radius 0.3039 m — REF §V4's independently stated 0.307 m, reached here without its ground line. The flat and the sidewall bulge are plainly visible at 4×.
findings.model_does: `t1_detail.tyre` is `T.revolve(prof, seg=112, axis='Y')` — axisymmetric, so a contact flat cannot be expressed in the profile at all. `build.py` step 7 places every wheel part at `D.place(o, loc=(x, s * tr / 2, T.TIRE_R))`, and step 8b's `_is_wheel` / `_WHEEL_PREFIX` exempts all 24 wheel parts from the shear, with the comment "circles resting on flat ground: contact patch at z = 0, centre at exactly TIRE_R". `studio.cyclorama` builds the catcher at z = 0. `verify._measure_wheels` returns TYRE_D = max(z) − min(z) and STATE.md prints it as 0.6650 — the free diameter exactly, which is the model confirming it has no flat.
findings.method: Free radius by three routes that share no edge (upper-arc rays 70.62 ± 0.08 sem, free circle fit 70.52, and the rim flange × the built TIRE_R/RIM_R 70.23) → 70.43 ± 0.25 px; contact row 668.5 ± 0.4 px; the ruler is the tyre's own free diameter (2 × 70.43 px ≡ 0.665 m → 211.8 px/m), so no external scale, no ground line and no projective correction enters. 28.6 ± 2.3 mm, plus ±0.6 mm carried from TYRE_D's own ±15 mm. ADJUDICATION OF THE FOUR LIVE VALUES: 35 ± 6 is refuted (AUDIT_rev12 §22 — a fixed L-band mask is a different edge criterion on every background); 27 ± 9 is not independent (same photograph, same red-dome centre, and it used the ground line); 31.7 ± 4 sits 0.8σ from this; and 23 ± 4 does not follow from the geometry AUDIT_rev12 published in the same paragraph — its own "R = 70.2–70.9 about the same centre, truncated at y ≈ 668.5" gives 6.18 px = 29 mm, not 23. So the four are one phenomenon, the honest consensus is 29 ± 3 mm, and the built value is the only value that is ZERO. CONSEQUENCE, and it is why this is also the ride-height answer: the model's hub is at the FREE radius 332.5 mm above z = 0 while the vehicle's is at the LOADED radius 303.9 mm, so the entire bus is lifted 28.6 mm bodily off its ground plane. Every ride-height number in the record — rev 13's rake solve, arch-lip-above-hub, rocker-above-hub — is referenced to the hub and therefore cancels this term by construction; it is invisible to all of them. CEILING: ±2.3 mm; the flat is 70 px long and 6 px deep in the worst-compressed frame in the set, and no sharper number exists without a sharper photograph.
findings.fix_location: build.py — step 7 wheel placement loop and step 8b `_is_wheel`/`_WHEEL_PREFIX` (a post-8b vertex deform, explicitly exempted from the shear); t1_detail.py:`tyre`. The guards that MUST move in the same edit, or verify goes off 0-fail on a correct change: verify.py:`_measure_wheels` TYRE_D and audit.py's 0.665 ± 0.015 check, which a 28.6 mm flat takes to 0.6364.

findings.title: The tyre is built ~150 mm in section against the 205–215 mm its own comment and REF's fitment identification require — and the constant is not even the one the mesh uses
findings.reference_shows: No frame in the set can measure a lateral section (see not-measurable). What the record shows: REF_MEASUREMENTS §V4 identifies the fitment from D = 0.665 on a 16-inch rim as 215/60R16 (0.664 m) or 205/65R16 (0.673 m), calling both "exact matches" — section 205–215 mm. SPEC §2's tyre row records "section ≈0.129", which is 215/60R16's SIDEWALL height (129 mm) mislabelled as its section width; the same row's own 0.665 diameter and 16-inch rim are what force 129 mm of sidewall.
findings.model_does: `t1_core.TIRE_W = 0.1550  # rev6: ~215 section on a 16in rim` — the comment states 215 and the constant is 155. Worse, the mesh does not read it: `t1_detail.tyre`'s profile reaches |y| = 0.0752, a 150.4 mm section, hard-coded. `TIRE_W` appears exactly once outside its own definition in the whole tree, in audit.py's track check `bhi.y - (T.TRACK_F / 2 + T.TIRE_W / 2)` — which therefore tests the mesh against a width the mesh never used, and is out by 2.3 mm for that reason alone.
findings.method: Source-side only, and stated that way. The 0.129/0.215 confusion is diagnosable exactly: 215/60R16 has a 129 mm sidewall and a 215 mm section, and SPEC §2 wrote the first under the second's name. This is the project's own named failure mode — a figure in a comment is not a measurement, and a constant that the geometry does not reference cannot be a lock. CEILING: which of 0.150 and 0.215 is right is NOT settled here. ref_side is broadside to within ~5° (rear rim ellipse a/b = 1.0033), where a 150 mm section projects to under 3 px; ref_workshop is a 3/4 with an uncalibrated ~4:1 perspective compression across the wheel; ref_rear34 is barred. findings.title: Ride height adjudicated: the bus IS lowered, the route is hub-referenced, and SPEC §0.2's bullet is a stale rev-4 entry that SPEC's own §2 row already overturned
findings.reference_shows: ref_side.jpg, rear wheel, u 700–800. The rear arch lip stands 78.98 px = 372.9 mm above the hub (lip from the R-channel edge, 13 columns u 720–780, v = 525.16 ± 0.49; hub from the 357-ray rim-flange circle fit at rms 0.339 px; ruler = the tyre's own free diameter). A factory 6.40-15 has R = 341.5 mm, so this arch would clear a FACTORY tyre by 31 mm. No road vehicle has 31 mm of static arch clearance. That is the whole argument and it needs no stock-gap figure at all; with REF's stock 90–120 mm it puts the body 59–89 mm down relative to its own axle. Over THIS tyre the same lip gives a 40.4 mm gap.
findings.model_does: SPEC §0.2, a list headed "Retired readings — regressions if they reappear", carries "⚠ bus lowered 65 mm / 110 mm — unsupported by any evidence. Stock ride height". SPEC §2's Ride height row, in the FROZEN front matter, says the opposite in the same file: "LOWERED. Rear arch-to-tyre gap 41 mm ... rev4 wrongly zeroed it ... Set RIDE_DROP = 0.065", tagged "rev4 said stock — WRONG", and the rev-6 changelog records "Rear arch gap corrected 71 → 41 mm". `t1_core.RIDE_DROP` is 0.0650. So §0.2's bullet, read literally, declares the shipped constant a regression.
findings.method: The two files do not disagree about a measurement — §0.2's bullet is the rev-4 verdict that rev 6 reversed and nobody struck, and REF §2's verdict is the one that survived. The substantive adjudication is that RIDE HEIGHT IS TWO TERMS AND NO SINGLE DATUM CARRIES BOTH. (a) BODY-ABOVE-HUB: measurable hub-referenced with no ground line — 372.9 mm here, against `ARCH_R` 373.5 built and LOFT_GROUND's 372.6 ± 5.2, and it is what rev 13's METHOD 4 anchored `RAKE_Z0`/`RAKE_DZDX` on. This term is RIGHT and it is what makes the bus lowered. (b) HUB-ABOVE-GROUND: this is exactly the tyre's loaded radius, it is 303.9 mm against the model's 332.5, and it CANNOT be seen by any hub-referenced measurement because it cancels out of all of them by construction — which is why 39 revisions of flank work never touched it. Finding 1 is term (b). CEILING: term (a) is ±2.5 mm here and its comparison to "stock" inherits REF's own 90–120 mm secondary figure, which is why the verdict is stated ORDINALLY (the arch cannot clear a factory tyre) rather than as a lowering in millimetres. The absolute drop versus a factory bus is NOT established by this and I do not publish one.

Concretely: even with a perfect model I could not have produced a corrected LID_OPEN_DEG to better than ±6°, nor any absolute roof or lid height at all; what I could and did produce is that its SIGN is wrong, which needs no ruler and is admissible where every ruler here is barred.

method_summary: Source read only; tree left clean (no Write/Edit, no build, no audit.py). Photographs measured with /tmp/blender/4.5/python/bin/python3.11 (numpy/PIL/scipy) from scratch scripts in the scratchpad, never in the repo. Model numbers taken by IMPORTING t1_core under that interpreter and evaluating its LUTs (ZB, ZT_ALL, RT_ALL, CR_ALL, RB_ALL, WX at the tail station) and by reading the literals in t1_shell.py (ENGLID_GAP, ENGLID_CUT_DX, GAPW, REAR_W/H/Z, roof_lids), t1_detail.py (PLATE_*, ENGLID_HANDLE_DROP, LOUV_*, FLAP_*, small_lamp) and build.py (TAIL_LAMP_OD, the commented bumper_r). Three techniques carried the work. (1) Sub-pixel trough fitting: column-averaged R-channel minima with a parabolic vertex, least-squares line fits with outlier rejection, used for the engine-lid shut lines. (2) A Radon-style de-rake: the louvre block's lines slope dy/dx = -0.032, which smears a full pitch across a 70-column row-mean, so I scanned slope, maximised high-pass contrast, then took the period by quadrature amplitude at 0.02 px resolution in three independent x-windows. (3) Ratio-only comparison: every number below is a ratio of two image extents measured within ~100 px of each other on the same panel, expressed in plate-outer-heights or as a fraction of the plate's own width. No ground line (SPEC 10.11), no px/m on the cab door plane (10.62/10.73), no cross-ratio, no harmonic conjugate, no probe_rev39_flank Z-ladder, no probe_v_apex anchor. The one metric scale I use is LOFT_GROUND_rev15's own local 226.9 ± 8 px/m at the tail panel, and only for the silhouette finding. On the frame's status: my brief says ref_rear34.jpg is SUSPECT under SPEC 10.15, but SPEC 10.19 — settled with the owner against marked crops — explicitly LIFTS that quarantine for the tail-end topology and the "1963" plate surround while keeping it on the lettered panel's placement. Every rear34 number here falls inside the lifted set; I say so rather than silently relying on it. I did not look in out/ and I describe no render.

findings.title: The flat tail panel is 0.996 m tall; the photograph's aft silhouette cannot be flat over more than 0.71 m
findings.reference_shows: ref_side.jpg, the tail's aft silhouette taken as the 50 %-crossing of the (R-B) step against the printed wall, column window x 860-1000. Rows 262-402 (cream, above the counter): 897 px at row 334, 902 at 350, 906 at 370, 913 at 398 — still climbing. Rows 402-465 are occluded by the counter fascia. Rows 466-590 (red): 917.6 at 474, 920.4 at 510, then 920.0-920.6 all the way to row 556, then 918.6 at 562, 916.9 at 570, 913.8 at 578, 908.4 at 584, 900.2 at 588. Flat to ±1 px over rows 492-560 (68 px); to ±3 px over rows 474-568 (94 px). Because the silhouette is measurably 7 px inboard at row 398 and 23 px inboard at row 334, the flat run cannot extend above row 398 — a hard bound of 160 px.
findings.model_does: t1_core's aft cap. Evaluated at the tail station the ring runs ZB = 0.4680 to ZT_ALL + CR_ALL = 1.4640, and t1_shell's loft closes it with cap_last, a planar disc at X_TAIL (the source's own notes confirm the Coons grid cap leaves the skin flat at X_TAIL). So the model's aft silhouette is flat over 0.9960 m by construction, with RB_ALL = 0.0850 and RT_ALL = 0.0820 as the only corner relief.
findings.method: Silhouette only — one edge locus per row, no datum. Converted with LOFT_GROUND_rev15's own local longitudinal scale at the tail panel (226.9 ± 8 px/m at u≈921), the flat run is 0.300 m at ±1 px and 0.414 m at ±3 px, with a hard upper bound of 0.705 ± 0.025 m. The upper bound is what carries the finding: the built 0.9960 m sits outside it by at least 0.29 m no matter where inside the occluded band the roll actually starts, so this converts LOFT_GROUND_rev15 sec.3.4's 'probably too tall, but I will not put a number on it' from a suspicion into a strict exclusion. Corroborated at the bottom end without any scale: the photograph's roll-under moves the silhouette 25 px inboard over the 34 rows from 556 to 590 and is still moving when it enters shadow, i.e. a roll-in of at least 0.118 m against RB_ALL's 0.085 m. Uncertainty: LOFT_GROUND's unbounded near-corner-versus-centreline bias (its own estimate < 15 mm) applies, and the ±8 px/m on the scale is 3.5 %. Neither touches the exclusion.
findings.fix_location: t1_core.py — the aft knots of ZT_ALL, ZB, RT_ALL and RB_ALL at the tail station (all consumed through aft_lut)

findings.title: The "1963" plate is 74 mm too low on the engine lid, which drops the T-handle off the lid onto the apron
findings.reference_shows: ref_rear34.jpg, near end (the TAIL, released from quarantine by SPEC 10.19). Engine-lid upper shut line fits y = -0.050592x + 627.715 (25 sub-pixel troughs, residual 0.31 px, x 1000-1192); it terminates at the vertical body line at x ≈ 983 rather than running on across the panel. Lower shut line fits y = -0.091215x + 849.079 (26 troughs, residual 0.44 px, x 996-1112, iterated outlier rejection). At the plate's centre station x = 1129.7 the lid spans y 570.56 to 746.03 (175.5 px) while the plate outer, from the build's own corner fit, spans 631.41 to 691.00 (59.60 px). The plate centre therefore sits 2.91 px = 0.049 plate-heights BELOW the lid centre. The chrome T-handle's centroid is at (1126.4, 737.2) — 9.2 px = 0.154 plate-heights ABOVE the lower shut line, i.e. plainly ON the lid.
findings.model_does: t1_shell.ENGLID_GAP is rrect(0.9400, 0.5000) offset to v + 0.8700, so the lid outline runs z 0.620 to 1.120. t1_detail.PLATE_Z = 0.7800 yields PLATE_OUTER_CZ = 0.78754, which is 0.4901 plate-heights below the lid centre — ten times the photographed offset and 74.2 mm low. t1_detail.ENGLID_HANDLE_DROP = 1.274 * PLATE_OUTER_H then puts englid_handle at z = 0.57322, which is 46.8 mm BELOW the lid's own lower shut line at 0.620; with the escutcheon revolve's 0.025 radius the whole assembly (englid_esc, englid_stem, englid_bar) lies between z 0.548 and 0.598, entirely off the opening panel and on the fixed apron.
findings.method: Ratios of vertical image extents on one panel, all within 180 px of each other: no px/m, no ground line, no vanishing point. Internal control that I am comparing the two objects the model builds: lid height / plate outer height is 2.944 measured against 2.972 built — 0.9 %. Robustness: a second horizontal groove exists at y = -0.055076x + 652.616; if THAT is the true upper shut line the plate is 102 mm low rather than 74 mm, and the handle still lands below the lid. So the systematic runs +28/-0 mm on top of about ±8 mm statistical, and the ordinal claim — the handle is on the apron in the model and on the lid in the photograph — survives either reading. The rev-15 handle ratio is not the fault and must not be touched: photographed handle drop / plate outer height is 1.274, built 1.274, exact. One change fixes both: PLATE_Z 0.7800 -> ~0.8543 puts the handle 27.5 mm above the lower shut line against a photographed 25.9 mm. Note this retires contradiction (b) as stated in my brief — the four conflicting AUDIT_rev12 / HANDOFF_rev13 numbers were superseded at rev 15/16 and the handle is now BELOW the plate as the photograph requires; the live defect is the plate's own anchor, not the handle's offset.
findings.fix_location: t1_detail.py — PLATE_Z (plate_1963 and englid_handle both inherit it through PLATE_OUTER_CZ)

findings.title: The trunk lid at the tail, owner-stated and open in the primary frame, is not built
findings.reference_shows: ref_side.jpg carries a cream-faced panel raked about 41 deg above horizontal, running from roughly (885, 293) to (1007, 187) in source pixels — about 162 px long — hinged at the roof's aft edge and standing up and back over the tail. It reads as a panel seen near edge-on (roughly 10 px of thickness against 162 px of length), it carries a dark band on its lower face and a red-tipped far edge, and the drip-rail bulb string continues along its lower edge onto it. SPEC 10.26's owner-settled panel table is what names it: the tail panel that is OPEN in ref_side.jpg and closed in ref_rear34.jpg is the trunk lid, artwork none.
findings.model_does: t1_shell.roof_lids builds exactly one lid — its docstring says so in terms ("The ONE cut roof lid, OPEN") and it emits lid_main, lid_board, lid_rail and lid_strut* and nothing else. There is no third panel and no aperture at the tail top. grep -c trunk t1_shell.py build.py returns 0 and 0, re-verified this pass.
findings.method: Presence versus absence at 6x on a contrast-stretched crop, plus a grep. No ruler is involved and none is needed. Ceiling, stated plainly: I can establish that a raked panel of roughly 0.77 m occupies that span in ref_side.jpg and that nothing in the source builds anything there, but the IDENTIFICATION of it as the trunk lid rests on SPEC 10.26's table, not on my own measurement — from the photograph alone it could be argued to be a prop or an awning arm, and its width and thickness are at the edge of what this frame resolves. I cannot say what its absence looks like in a hero because no render is reachable.
findings.fix_location: t1_shell.py — roof_lids (and the matching cut, alongside engine_lid_gap)

findings.title: The rear-quarter louvre block has twelve slots, not ten, and the built block is two slots short
findings.reference_shows: ref_side.jpg, louvre block x 777-834 at the comb's 50 %-amplitude crossings (visible to about 767-842 at 6x), y 440.8-490.0. De-raked at dy/dx = -0.032 from a Radon scan, the vertical high-pass has its dominant period at 4.46 ± 0.06 px in all three independent x-windows I tried (full 768-840, left half, right half) with amplitude 7.4-8.2 DN, plus a sub-harmonic at 9.3-9.7 px which is the alternating slot depth. Twelve troughs fit 440.75 + k*4.477 with every residual under 0.5 px. 49.25 px of block span / 4.477 px = 11.00 intervals, i.e. twelve slots.
findings.model_does: t1_detail sets LOUV_N = 10 with LOUV_Z_TOP = 1.0850, LOUV_Z_BOT = 0.8950 and LOUV_PITCH = (top - bot)/9 = 21.11 mm, and louvres() sweeps that comb on both flanks. In this photograph that comb's period is 49.25/9 = 5.472 px, whose quadrature amplitude is 1.3-2.4 DN — three to six times weaker than the measured fundamental, in every window.
findings.method: Pitch and block span are both pixel quantities in one image, so the count is their ratio and is dimensionless — no scale enters at any point. This ADJUDICATES contradiction (a) and explains both sides of it. REF sec.7's "7 clear slots, probably 7-9" came from a raw row-mean over columns 770-840; at -0.032 slope that window drifts 2.24 px, half a pitch, which smears the comb — de-raking is the whole difference. The catalogue "10 per side" in SPEC sec.4 is not what this vehicle shows. The built PITCH is in fact right and should be kept: 4.477 px at REF's own 211.5 px/m is 21.2 mm against the built 21.11 mm. The defect is the block EXTENT — nine intervals built against eleven measured, so LOUV_Z_TOP is about 42 mm low and two slots are missing off the top. Ceiling: the block's top trough sits only 3.8 px below the counter fascia's lower edge, so twelve is a FLOOR, not a ceiling — further slots could hide behind the counter. And the count assumes one dark line per slot; the 9.05 px sub-harmonic admits a six-slot reading, but that requires the intervening troughs to be a second feature, and in the unshaded upper half of the block (y 440-467) the two interleaved sets have comparable depth and a single uniform 4.48 px spacing. Ten is excluded under every reading.
findings.fix_location: t1_detail.py — LOUV_N and LOUV_Z_TOP (consumed by louvres)

findings.title: The "1963" lettering is half size — 48 % of the plate's width photographed against 22.4 % built
findings.reference_shows: ref_rear34.jpg. Sampling the plate's top rail along the frame's own bilinear parametrisation (from the build's four sub-pixel corners), the rail luma has a 55 DN baseline with four bright groups at s = 0.275-0.335, 0.355-0.470, 0.500-0.610 and 0.650-0.755 of the outer width, peaking 83-91 DN. So the lockup runs s 0.28 to 0.76 — 48 % of the plate's outer width — centred at s = 0.52, with a group pitch of 0.132 of the plate width. The frame's interior below the rail is empty red, as SPEC sec.4 says.
findings.model_does: t1_detail.plate_1963 lays the four digits at cy = (i - 1.5) * 0.0210 with a digit box 0.0110 wide, inside PLATE_W = 0.3300. The lockup therefore spans 0.074 m = 0.224 of the plate width at a pitch of 0.0636 — a little over half the photographed extent and pitch. The digit HEIGHT is correct and should not be touched: _PD_H / _PR_TOP = 0.553 built against 0.54 measured.
findings.method: A fraction of the plate's own width, so foreshortening, depth, camera pose and px/m all cancel identically — this is the same class of construction the build itself used for PLATE_ASPECT, minus the wheel protractor. Ceiling: each digit spans about 13 px here, so the glyph FORMS are not resolvable and I make no claim about them — only the lockup's extent, centre and pitch. The bright groups are taken to be the lettering rather than chrome glints; SPEC sec.4 and the owner-settled 10.19 both state the surround reads "1963", and four evenly pitched groups across the rail's centre is the signature of four digits, but that is an inference and not a segmentation.
findings.fix_location: t1_detail.py — plate_1963 (the 0.0210 digit pitch and the 0.0110 digit width passed to _seg_bars)

findings.title: The tail lamp is a surface of revolution; the photographed lens is a stadium, and SPEC sec.4 says oval
findings.reference_shows: ref_rear34.jpg, near tail lamp, segmented at the 50 % crossing between the lens core and the adjacent paint: bounding box y 650-713 (64 px) by x 926-967 (42 px), centroid (946.8, 682.1), 2107 px of area. Its row-width profile holds 38-40 px flat over y 668-698 — 47 % of its height — and is still 33-34 px at ±22.5 px from centre, where an ellipse inscribed in the same box predicts 30 px. That is 11-13 % fuller than an ellipse at both ends, on three sampled rows each side. A vertical luma cut at x = 947 shows the chrome bezel as bright rings at y ≈ 650 and y ≈ 709 with the dark lens between.
findings.model_does: build.py builds the pair from D.small_lamp, which is T.revolve about X — a surface of revolution, circular in its own plane — flipped in x and placed as a disc normal to -X at (X_TAIL + 0.0040, ±0.6200, 0.8250), i.e. facing straight aft on the flat rear plane. A surface of revolution projects to an ELLIPSE under any perspective and from any viewpoint; it cannot project to the observed stadium. Separately, SPEC sec.4's required detail inventory says "oval tail lamps".
findings.method: The ellipse test is pure shape and needs no scale, no depth, no turn angle and no camera pose, because every plane section of a solid of revolution is a conic. Un-compressing the horizontal on the flat rear plane by the build's own wheel-derived k = 1.1894 gives a true lens aspect of 1.28 : 1 tall against the built 1.00. Ceiling: the +11-13 % end-fullness rests on three rows a side and on where the segmentation threshold falls, so it is a modest signal; and the 1.28 : 1 figure additionally assumes the lens lies on the flat rear plane, which is exactly where the build itself puts it — if it actually sits on the corner roll the true aspect lies somewhere in 0.83-1.28 and only the ellipse test survives. Note also that plate_1963's docstring offers the lamp as a CONTROL by assuming it is round and then observing that the implied turn falls between the two plane bounds; that is not a test of roundness, since any oval in that range passes it equally.
findings.fix_location: t1_detail.py — small_lamp (called for tail{s} in build.py; needs an elliptical or stadium section, not a revolve)

findings.title: The engine lid is a bare sheet — the photograph's pressed relief inside the shut line is not built
findings.reference_shows: ref_rear34.jpg, inside the lid's own shut lines, two features. First, a second horizontal groove fitting y = -0.055076x + 652.616 (25 sub-pixel troughs, residual 0.25 px, x 1000-1192), lying 19.8 px = 0.33 plate-heights below the upper shut line and terminating at the same vertical body line (x ≈ 983) that the upper shut line does — I checked leftward and the trough depth collapses from 7.7 DN at x = 984 to 2.2 DN at x = 978, so it stops there rather than crossing the panel. Second, a large rounded-corner pressed boundary whose top-left corner sits near (1054, 618), 71 px inboard of the left shut line and 44 px below the upper one, its left edge running down to about y = 740.
findings.model_does: t1_shell.engine_lid_gap cuts a single gap_prism of width GAPW = 0.0055 along ENGLID_GAP and nothing more. grep for "recess" across t1_shell.py and t1_detail.py returns nothing, and t1_detail.spec4_details adds only plate_1963, plate_digits and englid_handle at the tail. The lid is a flat sheet with one groove around its perimeter.
findings.method: Sub-pixel trough fitting for the groove and its termination; the inner boundary located by eye at 5x on a difference-of-Gaussians crop. Scaled with the plate as the ruler on the same panel (outer 97.96 x 59.60 px = 0.330 x 0.16823 m), the inner boundary is inset roughly 0.24 m from the left shut line and 0.12 m below the upper one. Ceiling: I can place these edges but a photograph cannot tell me how DEEP the pressing is, so no profile can be derived here — only the plan positions. And I cannot fully exclude that the inner rounded boundary is a reflection rather than a pressing; the evidence that it is a pressing is its appearance at 5x as a continuous line with a tool-radius corner, which is a judgement and not a measurement. What is NOT in doubt is that two distinct linear features lie inside the shut line and the source builds neither.
findings.fix_location: t1_shell.py — engine_lid_gap (or a new pressed-relief detail in t1_detail.spec4_details)

findings.title: TAIL_LAMP_OD was set from an image-height ratio across 183 px of depth with no depth correction
findings.reference_shows: ref_rear34.jpg. The build's own plate corner fit measures the frame's near (left) vertical edge at 60.08 px and its far (right) at 58.72 px over a 97 px baseline — a measured depth taper on the very panel in question. The lamp centroid sits at x = 946.8 and the plate centre at x = 1129.7, so the lamp is 183 px nearer along that gradient. Propagating the plate's own taper (1/h affine in image x) to the lamp's station gives a plate outer height of 62.06 px there, not the 59.40 px measured at the plate.
findings.model_does: build.py sets TAIL_LAMP_OD = 1.1627 * D.PLATE_OUTER_H, from a docstring stating "lamp vertical D / plate outer H = 1.1627 +/- 0.0271 photograph" — the lamp's raw image height over the plate's raw image height, taken at their own separate stations. Depth-matched, my 50 %-crossing segmentation gives 64 px (bezel rings at 650 and 709 put the outer extent near 65-67 px) against 62.06, i.e. 1.03-1.08; the build's own 69.06 px gives 1.11. The built lamp is therefore roughly 5-12 % oversize at 0.19560 m.
findings.method: This is a method flag, not a number to apply, and it is the same shape as the bumper standoff that put the blade 63 mm proud of the nose crown: two figures compared across different datums. Ceiling: the taper the correction rests on is the same one the build's docstring itself calls "only ~1.2 sigma", so the correction is 4.5 % with about ±4 % of its own uncertainty; and my 64 px disagrees with the build's 69.06 px by 8 % purely because we threshold the bezel differently. So the correct statement is that the ratio is biased HIGH by an uncorrected depth term of about 4.5 %, not that the lamp is exactly 12 % large. Recorded separately because it is right: the lamp's Z and Y are fine — the photograph puts the lamp centre 0.1745 plate-heights below the lid centre, i.e. z 0.841 against the built 0.8250, and its lateral offset from the plate reads 0.59-0.62 m against the built 0.6200.
findings.fix_location: build.py — TAIL_LAMP_OD (the 1.1627 coefficient)

not_measurable.title: Where the rear window sits on the tail
not_measurable.why: No frame adjudicates it. In ref_rear34.jpg the whole rear-window band is behind the counter and its cream fascia; in ref_side.jpg the tail is edge-on. I record the source arithmetic so the next revision can act if a fourth frame ever arrives: t1_shell's REAR_Z = 1.4500 with REAR_H = 0.3400 puts the aperture's top at z = 1.620, which is 156 mm above the tail cap's own top edge (ZT_ALL + CR_ALL = 1.4640 at the tail station), so nearly half the window is cut into the roll-down rather than into the flat panel. Whether that is wrong needs a photograph, and there is none. It is also entangled with the flat-panel finding above and must not be moved before that is settled.

not_measurable.title: The fuel filler flap
not_measurable.why: t1_detail places FLAP_X, FLAP_Z, FLAP_W, FLAP_H on the -Y quarter — the off side. Neither in-service frame shows that flank and ref_workshop.jpg is a front three-quarter that does not reach it. The source already labels the station and height INFERRED, and nothing I can measure changes that.

not_measurable.title: The engine lid's hinge
not_measurable.why: No hinge geometry exists anywhere in the source, and all three frames show the lid shut. A photograph of a closed lid cannot resolve hinge type or position, so I make no claim either way.

not_measurable.title: The engine lid's width
not_measurable.why: The lid's left shut line is at x ≈ 983 and its right edge lies past the frame's right border at x = 1200, so only the height and the left edge are measurable. The built 0.940 m is CONSISTENT with the plate lying at the lid's horizontal centre (that predicts a 279 px image width against 293 px implied by the left shut line and the plate centre, a 5 % agreement), but that is a consistency check, not an independent measurement, and I will not report it as either a pass or a defect.

not_measurable.title: The louvres' section — proud lip or recessed slot, and the aperture
not_measurable.why: LOUV_PROFILE's 8 mm proud, 11 mm section and the source's own "~7 mm aperture (INFERRED -- 1.5 px, below the photograph's resolution)" sit under this frame's resolving power. At 4.48 px pitch only the comb's period, phase and extent survive; the cross-section does not. LOUV_OFF's 2 mm ride is likewise unmeasurable here.

not_measurable.title: The folk art on the rear quarter
not_measurable.why: Its dark-brown curlwork mass is authored in folk_gen (FLANK_MASSES MASS-R1, aft end -2.007 in the AUTHORED frame) and delivered by a box projection in t1_mats, and folk_gen carries its own re-derived _aft() for the rev-16 tail re-space. Establishing whether that projection actually lands the mass correctly on the re-spaced quarter is a UV and livery question for probe_rev42_uv's instruments, not a tail measurement. Duplicating it from a flank crop is exactly the route that produced the 0.0-0.2 % coverage error, so I stopped rather than guess.

not_measurable.title: How any of this looks
not_measurable.why: There is no hero and no reachable out/ artefact of the shipped build in this tree. Every finding above is a comparison between the SOURCE and a PHOTOGRAPH. I have not described a render and cannot. Note for the record that the rear bumper needed no photograph: build.py's bumper_r call is commented with SPEC rev6 sec.2.4's reason and bumper_irons is front-only, so the removed rear bumper is correctly absent and I have not re-opened it.

not_measurable.title: The glyph forms of "1963"
not_measurable.why: Each digit spans about 13 px of the plate's top rail in ref_rear34.jpg. That is enough to fix the lockup's extent, centre and pitch (reported above) and nothing else. Whether the real digits are seven-segment, embossed, or a conventional face — and therefore whether _seg_bars is the right generator at all — cannot be settled from any frame in this tree.

ceiling_statement: The ceiling on this dimension is set by the two photographs and by the absence of a render, not by care. Best case: (a) The plate-versus-lid offset is limited by which of the two candidate upper lines is the lid's shut line — my reading (lid height / plate height 2.944 measured against 2.972 built, 0.9 %) strongly favours the upper one, but the alternative moves the answer from 74 mm to 102 mm, so the metric cannot be tightened past +28/-0 mm systematic on about ±8 mm statistical. The ORDINAL half of it — the T-handle is 47 mm below the lid's lower shut line in the model and 26 mm above it in the photograph — is not subject to that and is as certain as the shut-line fits (residuals 0.31 and 0.44 px). (b) The louvre count is capped at a FLOOR of twelve, because the block's top trough sits 3.8 px below the counter fascia and slots above it cannot be excluded; and it presumes one dark line per slot, which the 9.05 px sub-harmonic leaves formally open even though the uniform depth in the unshaded upper half argues against it. Ten is excluded under every reading; the exact count is not settleable from this frame. (c) The flat tail panel resolves only to an interval — 0.30 to 0.41 m most likely, hard upper bound 0.705 ± 0.025 m — because the counter fascia occludes rows 402-465 and shadow swallows the roll below row 590. What that interval CAN do, and this is the point, is exclude the built 0.996 m outright. (d) The tail lamp's true aspect cannot be pinned without knowing the local surface normal on the corner roll; only the ellipse-versus-stadium test, and the fact that the build itself mounts the lamp normal to -X on the flat plane, are frame-independent. (e) ref_rear34.jpg carries SPEC 10.15's mis-identification history; SPEC 10.19 lifts the quarantine for exactly the tail-end topology and plate surround these findings rest on, and every number here falls inside that lifted set — but if 10.19 is ever reopened, findings 2, 5, 6, 7 and 8 fall with it. (f) Nothing here can tell you what a hero looks like. No render exists in this tree, and a perfect model of this dimension would still leave the question of how the tail reads under the studio lighting entirely unaddressed.
